$comment: Single source of truth for every environment variable this app reads.
Derived from the actual call sites, not from memory: `process.env.X` inside
convex/ means the var must exist on the CONVEX deployment; `process.env.X`
inside src/ means it must exist on VERCEL (server); `import.meta.env.VITE_X`
means it is baked into the CLIENT bundle and is therefore PUBLIC.
convex:dev        set on the dev Convex deployment
convex:prod       set on the prod Convex deployment
convex:defaults   set as a Convex PROJECT default, so each new preview
deployment inherits it (preview backends are created
empty and share nothing with prod)
Vercel environments. Setting a var on Production ONLY is
what makes preview deployments 500 during SSR.
Check the live systems: node scripts/check-env.mjs --remote

vars.name: VITE_CONVEX_URL
vars.note: Read by src/convex.ts in the browser. Once the Vercel build runs `npx convex deploy --cmd-url-env-var-name VITE_CONVEX_URL`, the deploy INJECTS this and you should not set it by hand on Vercel. Still needed locally, where `npx convex dev` writes it into .env.local.

vars.name: CONVEX_URL
vars.note: Server-side preference in src/routes/api/*. Falls back to VITE_CONVEX_URL, then to http://127.0.0.1:3210, so a missing value degrades silently to localhost in production — set it or rely on the injected VITE_CONVEX_URL.

vars.name: CONVEX_SITE_URL
vars.note: Read by convex/auth.config.ts. Convex sets this automatically on every deployment — do NOT set it yourself.

vars.name: SITE_URL
vars.note: Convex-only. Used for email OTP links (convex/ResendOTP.ts) and the Polar portal return URL (convex/users.ts). Defaults to https://buildsync.co.il, so a wrong value sends users to the wrong host rather than failing loudly.

vars.name: AUTH_RESEND_KEY
vars.note: Convex-only. Resend key used by the auth email OTP provider.

vars.name: RESEND_API_KEY
vars.note: Convex-only, OPTIONAL. convex/support.ts falls back to AUTH_RESEND_KEY, because both are plain Resend API keys for the same account and the same verified domain (buildsync.co.il) — Resend scopes keys by domain, not by sender address. Set this only if you want a separate key for support mail that can be rotated independently of auth mail. It was unset for the whole life of the project, which silently disabled every support-ticket notification.

vars.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
vars.note: Convex-only. Recipient for support notifications; defaults to support@buildsync.co.il.

vars.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
vars.note: Vercel server only, for the AI quote extract/compare routes.

vars.name: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN
vars.note: DUAL HOME. Vercel needs it for checkout + webhook; Convex needs it for the customer portal URL (convex/users.ts). Rotating it means updating BOTH systems.

vars.name: POLAR_SERVER
vars.note: DUAL HOME, and it must MATCH across both: src/server/billing/products.ts picks the plan→product id map from it while convex/users.ts builds the portal from it. A mismatch silently points checkout and portal at different Polar environments. Required ONLY in the production homes — everywhere else the code's 'sandbox' default is deliberate, because local development forwards webhooks with `polar listen http://localhost:3000/api/webhook/polar` against the Polar sandbox. Its absence from convex:dev is intentional, not drift.

vars.name: POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET
vars.note: Vercel server only. src/routes/api/webhook/polar.ts asserts it non-null with `!`, so a missing value is a runtime crash on webhook delivery.

vars.name: SUBSCRIPTION_SYNC_SECRET
vars.note: DUAL HOME and must be BYTE-IDENTICAL in Convex and Vercel. The Polar webhook route sends it; convex/users.ts compares it. If they differ, subscription sync fails silently and paid users keep free-tier entitlements. check-env.mjs compares sha256 hashes so a mismatch is detectable without printing the secret.

vars.name: VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
vars.note: Convex-only (convex/pushActions.ts). MUST equal VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY — the browser subscribes with the client copy and Convex signs with this one, so a mismatch makes every push silently fail.

vars.name: VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY
vars.note: Convex-only. The signing half of the VAPID pair.

vars.name: VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
vars.note: Client bundle (src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts). Public by design; must equal VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY.

vars.name: E2E_EMAIL
vars.note: Playwright only. Lives in the git-ignored .env.e2e. Dev/local accounts only — never a production user.

vars.name: E2E_PASSWORD
vars.note: Playwright only, from .env.e2e.

vars.name: E2E_BASE_URL
vars.note: Optional. Points Playwright at a deployed URL instead of a local server.

vars.name: E2E_BUILD_PORT
vars.note: Optional. Port for playwright.build.config.ts; defaults to 3100, deliberately not 3000 so a running dev server can never be tested by mistake.

vars.name: NODE_ENV
vars.note: Set by the tooling. src/server/billing/products.ts uses it to pick the default Polar server.

vars.name: VERCEL_ENV
vars.note: Vercel-provided: 'production' | 'preview' | 'development'. Read by src/utils/envGuard.ts so a missing-variable error can name which environment it happened in.

vars.name: VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA
vars.note: Vercel-provided. vite.config.ts bakes it into VITE_BUILD_ID.

vars.name: VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID
vars.note: Vercel-provided. Fallback for VITE_BUILD_ID.

vars.name: CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY
vars.note: Not read by app code — consumed by `npx convex deploy` in the Vercel build. Needs TWO separate entries under the same name: a Production deploy key scoped to the Production environment only, and a Preview deploy key scoped to Preview only. The Preview key is what gives each branch its own Convex backend.
